title: Java Annotations
learningObjectives: Explain how annotations provide metadata to compilers and tools
Use Override and Deprecated annotations appropriately in Java code
Declare custom annotation types using the @interface syntax
Select annotation targets and retention policies for a use case
Inspect runtime-retained annotations using Java reflection

understand.concept: Annotations provide metadata for compilers, tools and runtime frameworks. Custom annotations use @interface; retention and target control where they apply.
understand.whyItMatters: Java Annotations helps learners create Java applications that are easier to reason about, test and maintain.
understand.analogy: Treat the concept as a clearly labeled tool for one programming responsibility.
understand.analogyLimit: Actual behavior is defined by Java language rules and API contracts.

explain.narrative:
## Annotation purpose

Annotations attach metadata to declarations such as classes, methods, fields, parameters and packages. The Java compiler, build tools, static analyzers, frameworks or runtime reflection can interpret that metadata. An annotation does not automatically change a method's behaviour merely because it is present.

## Built-in annotations

@Override asks the compiler to verify that a method overrides or implements a method from a supertype. @Deprecated marks an API as discouraged for new use and can include a removal warning. @SuppressWarnings requests suppression of selected compiler warnings; keep its scope as narrow as possible so useful diagnostics remain visible.

## Declaring custom annotations

Use @interface to declare an annotation type. Annotation elements resemble no-argument methods and may have permitted primitive, String, Class, enum, annotation or one-dimensional array types. Elements can declare default values. Apply meta-annotations such as @Target to restrict where the annotation may appear and @Retention to define how long it is retained.

## Retention policies

SOURCE annotations are discarded by the compiler. CLASS annotations are recorded in the class file but are not required to be available through runtime reflection. RUNTIME annotations remain available to reflection. The default retention is CLASS when @Retention is omitted.

## Inspecting annotations

For a runtime-retained annotation, reflection methods such as Class.getAnnotation can retrieve its metadata. Check for null when an annotation may not be present. Reflection reads metadata; it does not itself execute the behavior described by that metadata.

## Practical cautions

Choose targets and retention based on the consumer. Avoid broad warning suppression, and do not mistake documentation or metadata annotations for access control or security enforcement.

examples.title: Core concept
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { System.out.println(Deprecated.class.isAnnotation()); } }
examples.explanation: @Deprecated is itself a built-in annotation type; applying it marks an API as discouraged and can produce compiler warnings at use sites.

examples.title: Practical use
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { class Example { @Override public String toString() { return "Example"; } } System.out.println(new Example()); } }
examples.explanation: @Override causes the compiler to check that the method really overrides or implements an inherited method signature.

examples.title: Boundary behavior
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { @SuppressWarnings("deprecation") String oldName = "legacy"; System.out.println(oldName); } }
examples.explanation: SuppressWarnings is scoped to the annotated declaration; keep the suppression narrow so unrelated warnings remain visible.

examples.title: Runtime annotation inspection
examples.code: public class Main { @java.lang.annotation.Retention(java.lang.annotation.RetentionPolicy.RUNTIME) @java.lang.annotation.Target(java.lang.annotation.ElementType.TYPE) @interface Marker {} @Marker static class Marked {} public static void main(String[] args) { System.out.println(Marked.class.isAnnotationPresent(Marker.class)); } }
examples.explanation: The custom annotation is retained at runtime and targeted to types, so reflection on the annotated class can retrieve its value.

examples.title: Class-retained annotation
examples.code: public class Main { @java.lang.annotation.Retention(java.lang.annotation.RetentionPolicy.CLASS) @java.lang.annotation.Target(java.lang.annotation.ElementType.TYPE) @interface CourseTag {} @CourseTag static class Course {} public static void main(String[] args) { System.out.println(Course.class.isAnnotationPresent(CourseTag.class)); } }
examples.explanation: CLASS retention records annotation metadata in the class file but does not make the annotation available through ordinary runtime reflection.

practise.guidedTask: Use @Override and @Deprecated in a small example. Declare a custom runtime annotation with @Target(TYPE), apply it to a class and inspect it with reflection.
practise.independentTask: Create a custom annotation with documented retention and target. Demonstrate how a runtime-retained annotation can be read with reflection.
hints: An annotation supplies metadata; it does not automatically implement the behavior it describes.
Choose SOURCE, CLASS or RUNTIME retention according to whether the compiler, bytecode tools or runtime reflection needs the metadata.
Use @Target to limit valid declaration locations and keep @SuppressWarnings as narrow as possible.
practise.challenge: Compare SOURCE, CLASS and RUNTIME retention. Explain why SuppressWarnings should be narrow and why annotations are metadata rather than automatic behavior.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of an annotation?
options: Attach metadata for compilers, tools or frameworks
Execute a method automatically in every case
questions.answer: Attach metadata for compilers, tools or frameworks
questions.explanation: Deprecated is a Java annotation type, so Class.isAnnotation reports true for the Deprecated annotation declaration.

questions.prompt: What does @Override ask the compiler to check?
options: That the method overrides a superclass or interface method
questions.answer: That the method overrides a superclass or interface method
questions.explanation: @Override asks the compiler to verify the method overrides a supertype method; the method then supplies the object's text representation.

options: The API is discouraged for new use and may be removed in a future release
questions.answer: The API is discouraged for new use and may be removed in a future release
questions.explanation: SuppressWarnings applies to the annotated declaration; this local suppression is limited to the intended deprecation warning.

questions.prompt: Which syntax declares a custom annotation type?
questions.explanation: The annotation has RUNTIME retention and TYPE target, so reflection can find it on the annotated class.

questions.prompt: Which meta-annotation controls where an annotation may be applied?
questions.explanation: CLASS retention stores annotation metadata in the class file but does not require it to be available through runtime reflection.
